name: GitLab Community Edition
tagline: A complete DevOps platform in one application
description: Git hosting, merge requests, issue boards, a package and container registry, Pages and one of the most capable CI/CD systems available, all in a single self-managed application.
licenseNote: The Community Edition is MIT-licensed. Many features (advanced approval rules, security scanning, portfolio planning and more) exist only in the proprietary paid tiers.

maturity.rationale: Fifteen years of monthly releases, with well-documented upgrade paths and self-managed installs at every scale.

selfHosting.summary: The Linux package or official Docker image installs everything in one go, and upgrades are well documented as long as you follow the prescribed version path. It is a large application: give it real hardware and it behaves.

requirements.notes: It can be tuned to run in less memory, but it is not happy there. CI runners need their own machines.

managedHosting.label: GitLab.com
managedHosting.note: Free tier with CI minute limits; paid plans per user

strengths: Mature built-in CI/CD that many teams prefer to GitHub Actions
The official GitHub importer brings repositories, issues, pull requests, comments and releases
Everything in one place: registry, Pages, environments, issue boards and wiki
weaknesses: Resource-hungry: 8 GB of RAM before your first repository
GitHub Actions workflows must be rewritten as GitLab CI pipelines
Open core, with many attractive features locked to paid tiers
